name: Customer Identification Policy
description: The formal governing instrument for customer identification at FirstUK Bank, version 2.1, effective from 2026-01-15. It is owned by the Head of Compliance and applies to all staff, branch managers, compliance, and risk personnel.

name: FCA COBS Part 10
description: A regulatory reference from the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Conduct of Business Sourcebook, Part 10, which informs the requirements of the Customer Identification Policy.

name: Money Laundering Regulations 2017
description: The primary UK legislation governing money laundering prevention that serves as a regulatory basis for the bank's customer identification procedures.

name: Head of Compliance
description: The abstract role designated as the owner of the Customer Identification Policy, responsible for its maintenance and oversight.

name: All Staff
description: The collective group of bank employees to whom the Customer Identification Policy is applicable.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Branch Managers
description: Staff members in management positions at bank branches who are subject to the requirements of the Customer Identification Policy.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Compliance
description: The compliance function/staff members responsible for ensuring adherence to the Customer Identification Policy.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Risk
description: The risk management function/staff members who are part of the target audience for the Customer Identification Policy.
context: Audience | All Staff, Branch Managers, Compliance, Risk

name: Customer Identification Policy (KYC)
description: A comprehensive governing instrument designed to ensure customer legitimacy and prevent financial crime. It establishes the mandatory procedures for identity and address verification at account opening and during periodic reviews.
context: FirstUK Bank maintains a comprehensive Customer Identification Policy (KYC)
This policy establishes mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter.

name: Mandatory Identity and Address Verification at Account Opening
description: A requirement that the bank must verify both the identity and the address of a customer at the point of account opening.
context: establishes mandatory procedures for verifying customer identity and address at account opening

name: Periodic Customer Identity and Address Refresh
description: A requirement to perform identity and address verification on a periodic basis following the initial account opening.
context: verifying customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter.

name: Financial Crime
description: The broad category of financial crime that the Customer Identification Policy is designed to prevent through the verification of customer legitimacy.

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: The operational process of verifying a customer's identity to ensure legitimacy and regulatory compliance.
context: verifying customer identity and address at account opening

name: Customer Address Verification
description: The operational process of verifying a customer's residential or business address as part of the KYC requirements.
context: verifying customer identity and address at account opening

name: Know Your Customer (KYC) Verification Policy
description: A formal policy establishing the procedures for verifying customer identity, address, and risk profiles. Its primary objective is to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and prevent the onboarding of sanctioned individuals or entities.
context: To establish procedures for Know Your Customer (KYC) verification
Prevent opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities

name: Mandatory Customer Identity Confirmation
description: A requirement within the KYC verification process to confirm the identity of the customer.

name: Mandatory Customer Address Verification
description: A requirement within the KYC verification process to verify the customer's address.

name: Mandatory Customer Risk Profile Assessment
description: A requirement to assess the risk profile of the customer as part of the KYC verification procedures.

name: Financial Conduct Authority Conduct of Business Sourcebook
description: The regulatory framework issued by the FCA that the bank's KYC verification procedures must meet.
context: Meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements

name: Money Laundering Regulations
description: The statutory regulations regarding money laundering that the bank's KYC verification procedures must comply with.
context: Meet FCA COBS and Money Laundering Regulations requirements

name: Sanctions Violation Risk
description: The risk of opening accounts for individuals or entities that are subject to sanctions.
context: Prevent opening accounts for sanctioned individuals or entities

name: KYC Verification Process
description: The overarching process of confirming identity, verifying address, and assessing risk profiles for customers.
context: establish procedures for Know Your Customer (KYC) verification

name: Customer Onboarding and KYC Policy
description: A formal policy governing the requirements for opening customer accounts, establishing new customer relationships, and performing periodic re-verification. It defines the scope of application for retail and joint accounts and specifies the staff involved in onboarding.
context: Applies to: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)
All staff involved in customer onboarding

name: Mandatory KYC for New Customer Account Openings
description: A requirement that all new customer account openings, specifically including retail and joint accounts, must undergo the onboarding process.
context: Applies to: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: Mandatory KYC for New Customer Relationships
description: A requirement that all new customer relationships established with the bank are subject to the policy's onboarding and verification standards.
context: Applies to: All new customer relationships

name: Periodic Customer Re-verification Requirement
description: An obligation to perform periodic re-verification of customer identities and information as defined by the bank's business ontology.

name: Onboarding Staff
description: All bank staff involved in the customer onboarding process who are responsible for implementing the requirements of the policy.
context: All staff involved in customer onboarding

name: Retail Account
description: Individual retail customer accounts subject to the onboarding and KYC requirements of the policy.
context: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: Joint Account
description: Accounts held by multiple customers that are explicitly within the scope of the onboarding and KYC policy.
context: All customer account openings (retail, joint accounts)

name: New Customer
description: Individuals or entities establishing a new relationship with the bank and therefore subject to the onboarding policy.

name: KYC Verification Process
description: The process of verifying customer identity, including the specific requirement for periodic re-verification.

name: FirstUK Bank Customer Identification and Verification Policy
description: The governing policy establishing the bank's requirement for the positive identification and verification of all customers prior to the commencement of a business relationship.
context: FirstUK Bank requires that all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision.

name: Mandatory Customer Identification and Verification Prior to Onboarding
description: A mandatory requirement stating that all customers must undergo positive identification and verification processes before an account can be opened or a product provided.
context: FirstUK Bank requires that all customers be positively identified and verified before account opening or product provision.

name: All Customers
description: Individuals or entities seeking to open an account or obtain a product who are subject to the bank's identification and verification requirements.
context: FirstUK Bank requires that all customers be positively identified and verified

name: Bank Customer
description: Any person or entity attempting to access bank services who must be verified before account opening.
context: FirstUK Bank requires that all customers be positively identified and verified

name: Bank Account
description: A customer account whose opening is contingent upon the successful completion of identification and verification processes.
context: before account opening or product provision

name: Banking Product
description: Any financial product provided by FirstUK Bank that requires the customer to be positively identified and verified prior to provision.
context: before account opening or product provision

name: Customer Identification and Verification Process
description: The process of positively identifying and verifying a customer's identity as a prerequisite for account opening or product provision.
context: all customers be positively identified and verified

name: Core Requirements Policy
description: A governing instrument defining the mandatory identity, address, and documentation standards for account opening and maintenance, including retention and review schedules.

name: Mandatory Identity Verification at Account Opening
description: A requirement that identity verification must be performed for all customers at the time of account opening.
context: Identity Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Mandatory Address Verification at Account Opening
description: A requirement that address verification must be performed for all customers at the time of account opening.
context: Address Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Physical Evidence Documentation Requirement
description: A mandate requiring that physical evidence be provided and collected as part of the documentation process.

name: Six Year Record Retention Rule
description: An obligation to retain records for a period of 6 years following the closure of a customer account.

name: Periodic KYC Review Schedule
description: A requirement for periodic reviews of customer data, occurring every 3–5 years for lower-risk customers and annually for high-risk customers.
context: Periodic Review: Every 3–5 years for lower-risk customers; annually for high-risk customers

name: Non-Standard Scenario Exception Process
description: A requirement that any non-standard scenarios must be escalated to the Compliance Head for approval.
context: Exception Process: Escalation to Compliance Head for non-standard scenarios

name: Identity Verification Process
description: The operational mechanism used to verify the identity of a customer during the account opening process.
context: Identity Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Address Verification Process
description: The operational mechanism used to verify the residential or business address of a customer during account opening.
context: Address Verification: Mandatory at account opening

name: Physical Document Collection
description: The requirement to obtain and store physical evidence as part of the KYC documentation process.

name: Compliance Head
description: The role responsible for reviewing and approving exceptions for non-standard KYC scenarios.
context: Escalation to Compliance Head for non-standard scenarios

name: High-Risk Customer Profile
description: A customer classification that triggers more frequent (annual) periodic reviews due to a higher risk profile.

name: Lower-Risk Customer Profile
description: A customer classification that allows for a longer periodic review cycle of 3–5 years.

name: New Account
description: An account in the process of being opened, subject to mandatory identity and address verification.

name: Closed Account
description: An account that has been terminated, triggering the 6-year record retention clock.

name: Identity Verification Procedures
description: A formal policy document outlining the acceptable documentation and verification methods required to establish the identity of both UK and Non-UK customers.

name: Primary Identity Document Verification for UK Customers
description: Mandates that UK customers must provide a valid, non-expired primary identity document, such as a passport, driving license, or national ID card, subject to specific check and verification methods.
context: UK Driving License — Valid, not expired, photocard
UK National ID Card — Valid, not expired (when introduced)

name: Primary Identity Document Verification for Non-UK Customers
description: Requires Non-UK customers to provide a foreign passport (with a preference for English-speaking countries), an EU equivalent driving license, or an EU equivalent national ID card.

name: DVLA Online Verification
description: An operational verification method used specifically for UK Driving Licenses to validate the document via an online check with the DVLA.

name: Direct Examination or Certified Copy Verification
description: The approved method for verifying UK Passports, requiring either the physical examination of the original document or a certified copy.
context: Verification method: Direct examination or certified copy

name: UK Customer
description: Customers residing or based in the UK who are subject to specific primary identity document requirements including UK Passports and Driving Licenses.

name: Non-UK Customer
description: Customers from outside the UK who must provide foreign or EU-equivalent identity documentation for verification.

name: Identity Verification Process
description: The overall process of collecting and verifying primary identity documents to ensure customers are who they claim to be.
context: Document check: Signature, photo, personal details
Document check: Photo, signature, address, driving record

name: UK Passport
description: An acceptable primary identity document for UK customers, provided it is valid and not expired.

name: UK Driving License
description: An acceptable primary identity document for UK customers, provided it is a valid, non-expired photocard.
context: UK Driving License — Valid, not expired, photocard

name: UK National ID Card
description: An acceptable primary identity document for UK customers, provided it is valid and not expired.
context: UK National ID Card — Valid, not expired (when introduced)

name: Foreign Passport
description: An acceptable primary identity document for Non-UK customers, with a stated preference for those from English-speaking countries.

name: EU Equivalent Driving License
description: An acceptable primary identity document for Non-UK customers that is equivalent to the EU standard.

name: EU Equivalent National ID Card
description: An acceptable primary identity document for Non-UK customers that is equivalent to the EU standard.

name: Identification Process Policy
description: A formal policy governing the identification process for customers, detailing the steps for document collection, physical verification, and system recording across different onboarding channels.

name: Mandatory Primary Document Collection
description: Requirement to request a primary document from the customer and collect specific metadata including document ID, issue date, and expiry date, while assessing for tampering.
context: Collect document ID, issue date, expiry date

name: Physical Document Verification Standards
description: Obligation to examine original documents or certified copies, verify photo and signature matches, and ensure the document is not expired.
context: Examine original document in person (branch opening) or certified copy (postal)
Verify photo matches customer appearance (if in-person)

name: System Recording of Identification Data
description: Requirement to record document details in the Account Management System (AMS), link to the identification document entity, and flag concerns for manual review.
context: Record document type, number, issue/expiry dates in AMS (Account Management System)
Flag any concerns for manual review

name: Branch Opening Verification Requirements
description: Highest assurance verification requiring physical examination of original documents, in-person photo verification, and specific recording of staff name and date.

name: Online Opening Verification Requirements
description: Medium assurance verification requiring notarized certified copies, automated validation where available, and manual review by Compliance staff.

name: Postal Opening Verification Requirements
description: Lower assurance verification requiring certified copies via registered mail, manual Compliance review, address cross-referencing, and recommended follow-up calls.
context: Customer sends certified copy by registered mail

name: Account Management System (AMS)
description: The technical system used to record document types, numbers, and dates, and to flag identification concerns for review.
context: Record document type, number, issue/expiry dates in AMS (Account Management System)

name: Automated Document Validation
description: A technical tool used during online account opening to validate uploaded documents.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Staff responsible for the manual review of identification documents for online and postal account openings.

name: Prospective Customer
description: The individual undergoing the identification process during account opening who must provide primary documentation.

name: Identity Verification Process
description: The end-to-end process of collecting, verifying, and recording customer identification documents across branch, online, and postal channels.

name: Primary Identification Document
description: The official document required from the customer, which must be checked for integrity, validity (expiry), and authenticity (photo/signature).

name: Address Verification Procedures
description: A formal set of procedures governing the acceptable documentation and verification standards for confirming a customer's residential address. It defines the hierarchy of primary and secondary evidence and the specific validity requirements for each.

name: Utility Bill Validity Requirement
description: Mandates that utility bills used for address verification must be current, dated within the last 3 months, match the customer's name and address, and be issued by major suppliers.
context: Requirement: Current bill (dated within last 3 months)
Check: Matches customer name and address

name: Council Tax Document Validity Requirement
description: Requires that council tax bills or banding notices must be for the current year and must match the customer's name and address.

name: Bank Statement Validity and Limitation
description: Requires bank statements from other institutions to be current (within 3 months) and show the name and address. It explicitly prohibits the use of a bank statement as sole evidence if the customer already holds an account with FirstUK Bank.
context: Limitation: Not accepted as sole evidence if customer has account with us

name: Utility Bill
description: A primary preferred document for address verification, including gas, electricity, water, or telephone bills.
context: Utility Bill — Gas, electricity, water, telephone

name: Council Tax Document
description: A primary preferred document for address verification consisting of a council tax bill or a banding notice.
context: Council Tax Document — Council tax bill or banding notice

name: Bank Statement
description: A primary preferred document for address verification, specifically statements from another bank.

name: Mortgage Statement
description: A secondary document used for address verification if primary documents are unavailable.

name: Tenancy Agreement
description: A secondary document used for address verification; must be signed and include landlord details.

name: Insurance Policy
description: A secondary document used for address verification, specifically buildings or contents insurance policies.

name: HM Revenue & Customs Correspondence
description: A secondary document used for address verification consisting of official correspondence from HMRC.

name: Electoral Register Extract
description: A secondary document used for address verification consisting of an extract from the electoral register.

name: Address Verification Process
description: The process of verifying a customer's residential address through the collection and checking of primary and secondary identification documents.

name: Address Verification Process
description: A formal procedure governing the steps required to verify a customer's address, including document collection, validation, and system recording.

name: Address Verification
description: The specific KYC process used to validate a customer's residency through document collection and format checking.

name: Address Verification Document
description: An official document requested from the customer to verify their residential address.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document

name: ID Document
description: A primary identity document used to cross-reference and compare address details against supporting documentation.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document

name: Mandatory Request for Address Verification Document
description: Staff are required to request a document from the customer specifically for the purpose of address verification.

name: Mandatory Recording of Document Metadata
description: Staff must record the specific type of document provided, the date of the document, and the address as it appears on the document.
context: Record document type, date, address shown

name: Address Cross-Verification Requirement
description: Staff must perform a comparison between the address listed on the primary ID document and the address listed on the supporting address document.
context: Compare address on ID document with address on supporting document

name: Jurisdictional Validation Requirement
description: Staff must confirm that the customer's address is located within the United Kingdom or another approved jurisdiction.
context: Confirm address is within UK (or approved jurisdiction)

name: UK Postcode Format Validation
description: Staff must verify that UK postcodes adhere to the specific format: A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2).

name: System Recording of Address Verification
description: The type and date of the address verification document must be formally recorded in the bank's system.
context: Record address document type and date in system

name: Business Ontology Linking Requirement
description: The recorded address must be linked to the Address entity within the bank's business ontology.

name: Discrepancy Flagging Obligation
description: Any inconsistencies or discrepancies found during the address verification process must be flagged in the system.

name: Address Recording System
description: The technical system used to store address document metadata, link to the business ontology, and flag discrepancies.
context: Record address document type and date in system

name: Risk-Based Customer Assessment
description: The governing framework for categorising customers into risk tiers based on demographic, geographic, and financial profiles to determine the level of due diligence required.

name: Low Risk Customer Classification Criteria
description: Defines the specific criteria for a customer to be classified as Low Risk, including age (18-65), UK nationality/address, use of standard products, and absence of adverse media, PEP status, or high-value transactions.
context:
Low Risk:
- Age 18–65
- UK national
- UK address
- Standard products (savings, current account)
- No adverse media
- Not PEP
- No high-value transactions

name: Medium Risk Customer Classification Criteria
description: Defines the criteria for Medium Risk classification, including age outliers, non-resident UK citizens, accounts exceeding £100k, professional/business status, or minor PEP connections.
context:
Medium Risk:
- Age >65 or <18 (>16 allowed for limited products)
- Non-UK resident but UK citizen
- Higher-value account (>£100k)
- Professional or business customer
- Minor PEP connections

name: High Risk Customer Classification Criteria
description: Defines the criteria for High Risk classification, including non-UK citizenship/address, significant PEP exposure, unclear beneficial ownership, risky transaction patterns, sanctions list matches, adverse media, or Compliance referral.
context:
High Risk:
- Non-UK citizen with foreign address
- Significant PEP exposure
- Beneficial owner unclear
- Transaction pattern suggests higher risk
- Country of residence on OFAC/sanctions list
- Adverse media identified
- Referred by Compliance

name: Low Risk
description: A risk tier assigned to customers meeting standard UK-based profiles with no red flags.

name: Medium Risk
description: A risk tier assigned to customers with specific attributes such as high account value or professional status that require moderate scrutiny.

name: High Risk
description: A risk tier assigned to customers with significant red flags, including sanctions list matches or PEP exposure, requiring enhanced scrutiny.

name: OFAC Sanctions List
description: The sanctions list issued by the Office of Foreign Assets Control used to identify high-risk jurisdictions and individuals.
context: Country of residence on OFAC/sanctions list

name: Compliance
description: The function responsible for reviewing customer profiles and referring them for High Risk classification.

name: UK National
description: A customer holding UK nationality, which is a criterion for Low Risk classification.

name: Non-UK Citizen
description: A customer who is not a citizen of the UK and possesses a foreign address, triggering a High Risk classification.

name: Politically Exposed Person
description: A customer with political exposure; minor connections lead to Medium Risk, while significant exposure leads to High Risk.

name: Professional or Business Customer
description: Customers operating in a professional or business capacity, classified as Medium Risk.

name: Higher-value Account
description: An account with a balance exceeding £100,000, which triggers a Medium Risk classification.

name: High-value Transaction
description: Transactions of a significant value; the absence of these is required for Low Risk classification.

name: Savings Account Product
description: A standard banking product that, when used exclusively, supports a Low Risk classification.

name: Current Account Product
description: A standard banking product that, when used exclusively, supports a Low Risk classification.

name: Adverse Media Check
description: The process of screening for negative news; identification of adverse media triggers a High Risk classification.

name: Beneficial Owner
description: The ultimate owner of the funds; if the identity of the beneficial owner is unclear, the customer is classified as High Risk.

name: Risk-Based Re-verification Policy
description: A policy governing the frequency of customer re-verification based on the assigned risk level of the customer.

name: Low Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandates that customers classified as Low risk must undergo re-verification every 5 years.

name: Medium Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandates that customers classified as Medium risk must undergo re-verification every 3 years.

name: High Risk Customer Re-verification Frequency
description: Mandates that customers classified as High risk must undergo re-verification annually or on a transaction basis.

name: Low Risk
description: A customer risk classification that requires the least frequent re-verification cycle.

name: Medium Risk
description: A customer risk classification requiring re-verification every 3 years.

name: High Risk
description: A customer risk classification requiring the most frequent re-verification, either annually or triggered by transactions.

name: Periodic Re-verification
description: The process of refreshing customer verification data at set intervals based on the customer's risk profile.

name: Risk-Rated Customer
description: Bank customers who are subject to different re-verification schedules based on their assigned risk level (Low, Medium, or High).

name: Anti-Money Laundering Policy
description: The governing policy document that defines the bank's requirements for AML screening and overall anti-money laundering frameworks.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A category of customer that triggers mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence due to increased risk profiles, such as residency in high-risk countries or PEP status.
context: Mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios

name: Politically Exposed Person (PEP)
description: A specific risk scenario where a customer is identified as a Politically Exposed Person, necessitating Enhanced Due Diligence.

name: Unclear Beneficial Ownership
description: A risk scenario where the ultimate beneficial ownership of a customer entity cannot be clearly established.

name: Unusual Transaction Patterns
description: A risk trigger based on financial activity that deviates from expected patterns, requiring enhanced scrutiny.

name: Fraud or Complaint History
description: A risk trigger based on a customer's previous history of fraud or formal complaints.

name: Regulatory Concern
description: A risk trigger arising from specific concerns identified by regulatory bodies.

name: Mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence for High-Risk Scenarios
description: A requirement that Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) must be performed for customers identified as high-risk or those meeting specific trigger scenarios.
context: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios

name: EDD Approval Requirement
description: A mandate that the Compliance Head must provide formal approval for customers subject to Enhanced Due Diligence.
context: Escalation: Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers

name: EDD Periodic Review Schedule
description: A requirement that EDD customers must undergo a periodic review at a minimum frequency of once per year.

name: Enhanced Identity Verification
description: The operational process of verifying a customer's identity using multiple documents as part of the EDD procedure.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification
description: The process of verifying the beneficial owners when the customer is an entity.
context: Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity)

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: The operational requirement to verify the origin of the funds provided by the customer.

name: Ongoing Transaction Monitoring
description: The continuous monitoring of transactions for EDD customers to detect suspicious activity.

name: Risk Assessment Documentation
description: The requirement to formally document the risk assessment performed for the customer.

name: Compliance Head
description: The role responsible for providing the final approval for customers designated as EDD.
context: Escalation: Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customers who meet trigger scenarios such as being a PEP or from a high-risk country, and are thus subject to EDD.
context: Mandatory for high-risk customers and certain scenarios
Compliance Head approval required for EDD customers

name: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Process
description: The comprehensive verification process including identity, beneficial ownership, and source of funds verification for high-risk customers.
context: Beneficial ownership verification (if customer is entity)

name: PEP Screening Policy
description: A formal policy governing the identification, screening, and management of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) to mitigate financial crime risks. It defines the scope of screening and the mandatory actions required upon PEP identification.

name: Politically Exposed Person Risk
description: The risk associated with customers who hold prominent public functions, including government officials, senior politicians, and military leaders, which may increase the susceptibility to bribery or corruption.
context: PEP = Politically Exposed Person (government official, senior politician, military leader, etc.)

name: Mandatory Screening of New Customers for PEP Status
description: A requirement to screen all new customers against PEP databases to identify politically exposed persons at the onset of the relationship.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases

name: Screening of PEP Family and Associates
description: An obligation to extend PEP screening to include the immediate family members and close associates of any identified Politically Exposed Person.

name: Ongoing Monitoring of PEP Status
description: A requirement to perform continuous monitoring to detect changes in a customer's PEP status over time.
context: Ongoing monitoring for PEP status changes

name: PEP Database Screening
description: The operational use of FCA/PRA lists, sanctions cross-references, and third-party data providers to identify PEPs.

name: Financial Conduct Authority PEP Lists
description: Lists provided by the Financial Conduct Authority used as a source for identifying Politically Exposed Persons.

name: Prudential Regulation Authority PEP Lists
description: Lists provided by the Prudential Regulation Authority used as a source for identifying Politically Exposed Persons.

name: Mandatory PEP Identification Actions
description: A set of mandatory steps to be taken once a PEP is identified, including system flagging, enhanced due diligence, and escalation.
context: Flag customer in system as PEP

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior official responsible for receiving escalations when a Politically Exposed Person is identified.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence for PEPs
description: A mandatory, more rigorous verification process applied to customers identified as Politically Exposed Persons.

name: PEP Screening Process
description: The process of checking new customers, their families, and associates against PEP databases and maintaining ongoing monitoring.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases
Ongoing monitoring for PEP status changes

name: PEP Customer
description: A customer identified as a Politically Exposed Person, including their immediate family and close associates.
context: Screen all new customers against PEP databases
Flag customer in system as PEP

name: Adverse Media Screening Policy
description: A policy governing the screening of all customers for adverse media, including criminal convictions and fraud allegations, to determine the materiality of the risk to the banking relationship.
context: Scope: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Mandatory Adverse Media Screening for All Customers
description: A requirement that all customers must be screened for adverse media, specifically looking for criminal convictions, fraud allegations, and sanctions violations.
context: Scope: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Adverse Media Response and Escalation Process
description: A mandatory four-step process when adverse media is identified: flagging for manual review, assessing materiality, escalating to the Compliance Head if material, and considering account rejection or enhanced monitoring.
context: 3. If material: Escalate to Compliance Head
4. Consider account rejection or enhanced monitoring

name: Criminal Convictions
description: Risk associated with customers who have a history of criminal convictions as identified through adverse media screening.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Fraud Allegations
description: Risk associated with customers linked to fraud allegations discovered during adverse media screening.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Sanctions Violations
description: Risk associated with customers involved in sanctions violations as identified through adverse media screening.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Adverse Media Screening Sources
description: The operational use of news databases, third-party screening providers, and regulatory announcements to identify adverse media.

name: Manual Review and Materiality Assessment
description: A manual control process to review flagged adverse media and assess its relevance and materiality to the bank's relationship with the customer.

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior role responsible for receiving escalations when material adverse media is identified during the screening process.
context: 3. If material: Escalate to Compliance Head

name: All Customers
description: The entire customer base of the bank subject to mandatory adverse media screening.
context: Scope: Screen all customers for adverse media

name: Adverse Media Check
description: The specific AML screening process used to identify criminal, fraud, or sanctions-related news regarding customers.
context: Screen all customers for adverse media (criminal convictions, fraud allegations, sanctions violations, etc.)

name: Documentation & Record Retention Policy
description: A policy governing the types of records that must be maintained for each customer, their storage location, access controls, and the mandatory retention period.

name: Mandatory Customer Record Collection
description: Requirement to maintain a comprehensive set of documents for every customer, including identity, address, KYC verification, risk assessments, and various screening results.
context: For each customer: Copy of identity document, Copy of address verification document, KYC verification record (date, method, approver), Risk assessment (if high-risk), PEP screening result, Adverse media screening result, AML screening result

name: Customer Record Retention Period
description: Mandate that all required customer records must be retained for a period of 6 years following the closure of the account.

name: Secure Document Management System
description: The designated secure technical system used for the storage of mandatory customer documentation.
context: Storage Location: Secure document management system (DMS-001)

name: Role-Based Access Control for Compliance
description: A security mechanism restricting access to the document management system exclusively to Compliance staff.

name: Access Audit Logging
description: A monitoring control ensuring that all access to customer records is logged for audit purposes.

name: Compliance Staff
description: The specific staff collective granted authorized access to the secure document management system.

name: Identity Document
description: An official document required to be copied and retained for every customer as part of the KYC process.

name: Address Verification Document
description: An official document required to be copied and retained for every customer to verify their residential address.

name: KYC Verification Record
description: The record of the KYC process, which must specifically include the date of verification, the method used, and the identity of the approver.

name: PEP Screening
description: The process of screening customers for Politically Exposed Person status, the results of which must be retained.

name: Adverse Media Screening
